name: Ahaziah of Israel
charge: Sending to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron, as though there were not a God in Israel
summary: Ahab’s son Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and sent to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether he would recover, and Elijah met the messengers with the Lord’s question: was there no God in Israel (2 Kings 1:2-3)? Two captains of fifty who ordered the prophet down were burned up by fire from heaven, and the third fell on his knees and begged for his life (2 Kings 1:9-14). Ahaziah died in his bed according to the word Elijah spoke (2 Kings 1:16-17).
offenseFull: After Ahab died, Moab rebelled against Israel (2 Kings 1:1). The nations David had subdued and put under tribute began to break away, because Israel no longer walked in the blessing that came from serving the Most High (2 Samuel 8:2). If Israel listened diligently and did His commandments, the Lord would set them on high and strike down their enemies before them; if not, they would be struck down before their enemies and their bodies left to the birds, the same judgment spoken on the house of Ahab (Deuteronomy 28:1, 7, 15, 25-26).

Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper chamber and lay sick, and he sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether he would recover (2 Kings 1:2). Baal-zebub is the lord of the flies, and the teaching calls him plainly Satan, a god of the Hamites at Ekron. It frames the act as a choice, like Joshua’s call to choose whom they would serve (Joshua 24:15): Ahaziah thought God was not listening and went to another nation’s god, and he could not blame God for that. He should have known the history. When the ark of God was brought to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out that it had come to kill them, and the hand of God was heavy there; the god of Ekron could not even defend his own people (1 Samuel 5:10-11).

The angel of the Lord sent Elijah to meet the messengers and ask whether it was because there was no God in Israel that they were going to inquire of Baal-zebub; the Lord’s word was that the king would never rise from his bed; he would die (2 Kings 1:3-4). Elijah was quick to the point, and left. The messengers described a hairy man with a leather belt, a man in a garment of hair like the camel’s hair John the Baptist later wore, and the king knew it was Elijah (2 Kings 1:7-8; Mark 1:6). Then he sent a captain with his fifty men, who found Elijah on top of a hill and told the man of God that the king ordered him to come down (2 Kings 1:9).
judgmentFull: Elijah answered that if he was a man of God, fire would come down from heaven and consume the captain and his fifty, and it did. The king sent another captain with fifty, who spoke the same way, and fire from heaven consumed them too (2 Kings 1:10-12). This is our history, not a Marvel movie: Elijah brought down fire three times, once on Carmel and then on the captains back to back (Ecclesiasticus 48:3). The Lord did not let His prophet’s words fall to the ground (1 Samuel 3:19). The third captain was a wise one. Having heard that a hundred men had been burned, he humbled himself quickly, went up, fell on his knees before Elijah, and begged that his life and the lives of his fifty be precious in the prophet’s sight (2 Kings 1:13-14). The angel of the Lord told Elijah to go down with him and not be afraid (2 Kings 1:15). The teaching draws the lesson: humble yourself and seek the prayers of the Lord’s leaders rather than scorning correction.

Elijah went to the king himself and delivered the same word: because he had sent to ask Baal-zebub as though Israel had no God to ask, he would never rise from that bed; he would die (2 Kings 1:16). He died according to the word of the Lord that Elijah had spoken, and since he had no son, Jehoram reigned in his place (2 Kings 1:17). The prophet brought kings to destruction and honored men from their beds (Ecclesiasticus 48:6). The same Ahaziah had joined with Jehoshaphat king of Judah to build ships, and because Jehoshaphat joined himself with a king who did very wickedly, the Lord broke the ships (2 Chronicles 20:35-37). If we join with the wicked, the Lord breaks our works.

lawsResolved.text: Divination, soothsaying, and the use of mediums, spiritists and occultists are forbidden practices.
We are not to listen to diviners, enchanters, mediums or sorcerers.
Those in government are not to consult mediums or spiritists for guidance but are to inquire of the LORD.
A man or a woman with a familiar spirit or who is a wizard shall be put to death.

text.text: And Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.

But the angel of the Lord said to Elijah the Tishbite, Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say unto them, Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron?
Then the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him: and, behold, he sat on the top of an hill. And he spake unto him, Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down.

And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, If I be a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
Again also he sent unto him another captain of fifty with his fifty. And he answered and said unto him, O man of God, thus hath the king said, Come down quickly.

And Elijah answered and said unto them, If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And the fire of God came down from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.

And he sent again a captain of the third fifty with his fifty. And the third captain of fifty went up, and came and fell on his knees before Elijah, and besought him, and said unto him, O man of God, I pray thee, let my life, and the life of these fifty thy servants, be precious in thy sight.
Behold, there came fire down from heaven, and burnt up the two captains of the former fifties with their fifties: therefore let my life now be precious in thy sight.

And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Forasmuch as thou hast sent messengers to enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron, is it not because there is no God in Israel to enquire of his word? therefore thou shalt not come down off that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.
So he died according to the word of the Lord which Elijah had spoken. And Jehoram reigned in his stead in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah; because he had no son.
Then Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.

And he smote Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground; even with two lines measured he to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And so the Moabites became David’s servants, and brought gifts.

And it shall come to pass, if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth:
The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.

But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee:
The Lord shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them, and flee seven ways before them: and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.
And thy carcase shall be meat unto all fowls of the air, and unto the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away.
